groups.title: Nitro Server Engine
groups.question: Your team may move the Nuxt app from a Node server to Cloudflare Workers, and every request needs a request id. Explain how Nitro supports this.

followUps.Nitro's Universal Deployment Model: How does Nitro deploy the same server code to different platforms?
followUps.Nitro Plugins and Server Middleware: What is the difference between a Nitro plugin and server middleware?

evidence.text: Nitro builds the server into a standalone output.
Presets target platforms like Node, Vercel or Cloudflare.
The same code runs on each, as long as it avoids platform-specific APIs.

notEnough: Only saying Nitro is the server engine.

evidence.text: Plugins run once at startup, for setup like database connections.
Middleware runs on every request.
A request id belongs in middleware, a database connection in a plugin.

groups.title: Server-Side Caching with Nitro
groups.question: A popular API endpoint hits the database for every request, and you need key-value storage that works locally and on Cloudflare. Explain Nitro's caching and storage.

followUps.Storage Layer with unstorage: What does Nitro's storage layer give you?

evidence.text: It wraps a route handler with caching.
Results are cached by request details like the URL.
The cache can use memory, Redis or other storage, with an expiry.
It offers one key-value API.
It works with backends like memory, Redis, files or Cloudflare KV.
The backend can change without changing the code.

groups.title: TypeScript in Server Context
groups.question: Your server routes trust whatever body they receive, and a secret API key was found in the browser bundle. Explain how you would type input and handle secrets.

followUps.Typed Request Bodies and Query Params: Why validate readBody and getQuery results?
followUps.useRuntimeConfig for Server Secrets: How does runtimeConfig keep secrets on the server?

evidence.text: readBody and getQuery return untrusted, untyped data.
A Zod schema validates and types it at the start of the route.
Invalid input is rejected with a clear error.
Keys in runtimeConfig outside public are server-only.
Only keys under public reach the browser.
Values can be overridden by environment variables at runtime.

groups.title: Node.js in Server Routes
groups.question: A server route that reads files works on Node but fails on an edge platform, and environment variables are read inconsistently. Explain the right patterns.

followUps.File System Access in Server Routes: Why does file system code break on edge runtimes?
followUps.Environment Variable Access Patterns: Why use runtimeConfig instead of process.env everywhere?

evidence.text: Node server routes can use fs and path.
Edge runtimes do not have those APIs.
Keeping file access in Node-only code or using the storage layer keeps the app portable.

notEnough: Only saying edge has no fs.

evidence.text: runtimeConfig is the standard way to read config in Nuxt.
It can be overridden by matching environment variables at runtime.
Reading process.env directly does not work the same on every platform.
